0.comment: Crucabena: Crucabena and the House of the Hearth contest
0.content: Under Crucabena the House of the Hearth looked like a family of kind adults and friendly children. She taught the children to fight, set them against each other in duels, and planned to crown the child who proved most worthy as "king" to inherit her title. The wounded who survived were sent to Dottore or on dangerous missions. She told stories of cruelty as if they were fairy tales.

1.content: Clervie was brought to the House at six to show the others that the Mother treated everyone equally; Arlecchino says Crucabena cared little for her. Clervie failed to change her mother's mind and tried to flee or expose the truth, earning beatings that were used as an example. Peruere proposed killing Crucabena, but Clervie refused because she still thought of Crucabena as her mother. Crucabena had Clervie duel Peruere, who killed her. Clervie died at sixteen; her shade, reverted to her six-year-old self and missing most of her memories, lingered until Arlecchino formally expelled her from the House in Into the Sunlight (4.6), freeing her to fade.
